title: Graphs I: BFS/DFS, Connected Components, Flood Fill, Topological Sort
relevance: High (grid/graph reachability, islands, bipartite checks, and course-order / dependency topo are OA staples)
company_notes: Grid islands / regions: count connected groups of 1s or flood-fill recolor from a click (Number of Islands / Flood Fill clones). Infection / minutes-to-spread: multi-source BFS until all fresh cells are reached (Rotting Oranges at Amazon/Meta-style OAs). Prerequisite / build order: courses or tasks with A before B; detect cycles and return a valid order (Course Schedule I/II). Reachability / walls: maze escape, blocked cells, or reach the border before X spreads — plain or racing BFS.

phases.goal: Establish that the candidate maps the prompt to graph/grid traversal, components, bipartite coloring, or topo/cycle signals.

must_hit.point: Model the input as an explicit graph (adjacency list) or an implicit one (grid 4-neighbors).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says build adj lists or treat the grid as an implicit graph with 4-neighbors.

must_hit.point: Connected components / flood fill answer how many regions, can A reach B, or min edges to connect.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps region-count / reachability / connect-with-min-edges wording to CC or flood fill.

must_hit.point: Topological sort is signaled by prerequisites, ordering constraints, or longest/number of paths in a DAG.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names prereq/order constraints or DAG path asks as the topo cue.

must_hit.point: Infection or minutes-to-spread on a grid (Rotting Oranges / Monsters-style) is multi-source BFS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps simultaneous spread / beat-arrival wording to multi-source BFS.

probes: Is this an explicit graph or an implicit grid graph, and is the ask regions, reachability, shortest unweighted path, bipartite, or ordering?
What wording makes you reach for flood fill, multi-source BFS, or topological sort?

hints.1: Ask whether neighbors are listed edges or grid cells, and what the ask counts or orders.
hints.2: Regions/reach/connect → CC/flood fill; spread from many starts → multi-source BFS; A-before-B / DAG paths → topo.
hints.3: Say: adj list or grid 4-neighbors; CC for regions/reach/min edges to connect; prereqs/order/DAG paths → topo; infection/minutes → multi-source BFS.

phases.goal: Choose DFS vs BFS vs Kahn/DFS-topo and state the component, bipartite, or cycle rule before coding.

must_hit.point: DFS explores deeply to mark a component, detect cycles, or color bipartitely; BFS explores by distance and is the default for unweighted shortest paths and multi-source spread.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts DFS for mark/cycle/2-color with BFS for distance and multi-source.

must_hit.point: Connected-component loop: for each unvisited node, run DFS/BFS and count or collect representatives.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes the outer scan over unvisited starts launching a traversal.

must_hit.point: Topological sort via Kahn indegree queue or DFS finish-order linearizes a DAG and fails exactly when a directed cycle exists.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Kahn or DFS finish-order and ties failure to a directed cycle.

must_hit.point: Multi-source BFS seeds the queue with all sources at dist 0; connecting C components needs C-1 edges.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Seeds every source at dist 0 and/or cites answer C-1 for C components.

must_hit.point: After a valid topo order, DAG DP processes longest path or path counts in topo order.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says run DP along the topo order for longest path or path counts.

probes: When do you pick DFS versus BFS here, and how do you start a connected-component count?
How do Kahn and DFS-topo detect a directed cycle, and when is multi-source BFS the right model?

hints.1: Separate deep mark/cycle/color work from distance or simultaneous spread.
hints.2: Outer unvisited loop for CC; Kahn/DFS-topo for order; seed all sources at dist 0 for infection.
hints.3: Say: DFS for component/cycle/bipartite; BFS for unweighted distance/multi-source; Kahn or DFS finish-order fails iff directed cycle; C components → C-1 edges; DAG DP after topo.

phases.goal: Code visited-safe DFS/BFS or flood fill, path reconstruction, 2-coloring, and Kahn or DFS-topo correctly.

must_hit.point: Adjacency-list DFS/BFS uses visited[]; iterative BFS uses a queue or deque.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions visited[] on an adj list and queue/deque BFS.

must_hit.point: Grid flood fill uses 4-dir deltas, bounds checks, and marks visited before enqueue or recurse.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes 4-dir deltas, bounds, and mark-before-enqueue/recurse.

must_hit.point: Unweighted shortest path stores BFS distances plus parent[] or a move char to reconstruct the path (including U/D/L/R on a grid).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes parent or move-char reconstruction after BFS.

must_hit.point: Bipartite check 2-colors with BFS/DFS; undirected cycle uses DFS with parent; directed cycle uses WHITE/GRAY/BLACK or failed Kahn.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates 2-color, undirected parent-DFS, and directed color states or Kahn failure.

must_hit.point: Kahn uses indegree plus a queue; if output size is < n, there is a cycle.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States indegree queue and output size < n ⇒ cycle.

probes: Walk through your flood-fill or BFS template—when do you mark visited, and how do you reconstruct a path?
How do you implement bipartite coloring versus undirected vs directed cycle detection, and Kahn's cycle signal?

hints.1: Start from visited[] / queue BFS and grid deltas with bounds.
hints.2: Mark before enqueue/recurse; keep parent or move char; 2-color; parent for undirected cycles; colors or Kahn for directed.
hints.3: Say: adj DFS/BFS + visited; 4-dir flood fill mark-before-push; BFS parent/U-D-L-R; 2-color; undirected DFS+parent; directed WHITE/GRAY/BLACK or Kahn; output size < n ⇒ cycle.

phases.goal: Tie traversal safety and topo templates to the scale and query pattern the file calls out.

must_hit.point: Marking visited before enqueue or recurse is required to avoid TLE and stack blowups on grid flood fill.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Links mark-before-enqueue/recurse to avoiding TLE/stack blowups.

must_hit.point: Kahn or DFS-topo templates must work at n ≤ 1e5 for contest Course Schedule–style graphs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites n ≤ 1e5 as the scale the topo template must handle.

must_hit.point: Precomputing per component (Igor-style) lets later queries answer in O(1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says flood-fill/memo once, then O(1) per query.

probes: What goes wrong on a grid if you mark visited too late, and what scale must your topo code handle?
When does precomputing a component answer beat recomputing per query?

hints.1: Think about revisit blowups and contest-size topo.
hints.2: Mark before enqueue/recurse; topo at n ≤ 1e5; optional component precompute for O(1) queries.
hints.3: Say: mark-before-push avoids TLE/stack blowups; Kahn/DFS-topo at n ≤ 1e5; precompute component aggregates for O(1) queries.

phases.goal: Surface mark-too-late, wrong cycle model, incomplete multi-source seeding, and missed Kahn cycle signal.

must_hit.point: Forgetting to mark visited before enqueue/recurse causes TLE or stack blowups on flood fill.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names late marking as the TLE/stack failure mode.

must_hit.point: Using directed-cycle machinery without a parent on undirected graphs, or skipping WHITE/GRAY/BLACK (or Kahn) on directed graphs, mis-detects cycles.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates undirected DFS+parent from directed colors or failed Kahn.

must_hit.point: Treating Kahn as always succeeding without checking that output size is < n misses the directed cycle.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says incomplete order / size < n means cycle / impossible.

must_hit.point: Seeding only one rotten/monster cell instead of all sources at dist 0 breaks multi-source BFS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists every source starts in the queue at dist 0.

probes: What fails if you mark a grid cell only after popping it from the queue?
How do undirected and directed cycle checks differ, and what does Kahn output size < n mean?

hints.1: Check when you mark visited and which cycle API you used.
hints.2: Mark before enqueue; undirected needs parent; directed needs colors or Kahn; seed every source at dist 0.
hints.3: Say: late mark → TLE/stack blowups; undirected DFS+parent vs WHITE/GRAY/BLACK or Kahn; output size < n ⇒ cycle; multi-source must enqueue all sources at dist 0.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use DFS to mark a component, detect cycles, or color bipartitely; use BFS when you need distances, unweighted shortest paths, or multi-source spread.

tradeoffs.topic: Explicit adjacency list vs implicit grid 4-neighbors
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Build an adjacency list when edges are given; on grids, treat cells as nodes with 4-neighbor edges and run the same DFS/BFS/flood-fill templates.

tradeoffs.topic: Kahn indegree queue vs DFS finish-order topo
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Both linearize a DAG and fail exactly on a directed cycle; Kahn uses indegree + queue (output size < n ⇒ cycle), DFS uses finish-order / color states (WHITE/GRAY/BLACK).

tradeoffs.topic: Plain CC flood fill vs flood fill + memo for queries
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Counting or marking components once is enough for region/reach asks; if many queries need the same component aggregate, precompute per component and answer in O(1).

gotchas.trap: Marking a grid cell visited only after dequeue/recurse instead of before enqueue/recurse.
gotchas.correction: Mark visited before enqueue or recurse to avoid TLE and stack blowups.

gotchas.trap: Detecting an undirected cycle without tracking the DFS parent (or treating it like a directed graph).
gotchas.correction: Undirected cycle: DFS with parent, reconstruct length ≥ 3; directed cycle: WHITE/GRAY/BLACK or failed Kahn.

gotchas.trap: Assuming a Kahn run always yields a valid order.
gotchas.correction: If output size is < n, a directed cycle exists and the ordering is impossible.

gotchas.trap: Starting multi-source BFS from a single source.
gotchas.correction: Seed the queue with all sources at dist 0 (rotten oranges / monsters).

gotchas.trap: 2-coloring only one component when checking bipartiteness.
gotchas.correction: 2-color every component with BFS/DFS; any conflict means impossible.
